chain_trace.break_detail: The log's DEFECT_FOUND (Type4) contradicts its own raw responses: the P3 batch was rejected as a whole (HTTP 400 at deserialization, before any operation executed) and point 502 was never created (GET 404) — i.e. NO half-apply occurred, which is precisely what the DEFECT message demands. The script's P3 oracle branch (state_points_batch_order_001.py:307-317) tests `st == 200` for the 'consistent rejection / upsert not applied / no defect' path whose message text describes the 404 case — the condition is inverted, so compliant atomic-rejection behavior was flagged as a violation. source_grounding.source_excerpt: src/common/update.rs:91-109 — #[derive(Deserialize, Serialize, JsonSchema, Validate)] pub struct UpdateOperations { #[validate(nested)] pub operations: Vec<UpdateOperation>, } / #[derive(Deserialize, Serialize, JsonSchema)] #[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")] #[serde(untagged)] pub enum UpdateOperation { Upsert(UpsertOperation), Delete(DeleteOperation), SetPayload(SetPayloadOperation), OverwritePayload(OverwritePayloadOperation), DeletePayload(DeletePayloadOperation), ClearPayload(ClearPayloadOperation), UpdateVectors(UpdateVectorsOperation), DeleteVectors(DeleteVectorsOperation), } — there is NO 'delete_points' variant; variant structs define the JSON keys, e.g. :262-265 pub struct DeleteOperation { #[validate(nested)] delete: PointsSelector, } (JSON key 'delete'). src/actix/api/update_api.rs:327-331 — #[post("/collections/{collection_name}/points/batch")] async fn update_batch(dispatcher: web::Data<Dispatcher>, collection: Path<CollectionPath>, operations: Json<UpdateOperations>, ...) — the whole request body is deserialized into Json<UpdateOperations> BEFORE the handler body runs; one failing element makes serde reject the entire request -> actix 400 'data did not match any variant of untagged enum UpdateOperation' with NO operation executed. src/common/update.rs:762-783 (do_batch_update_points) — 'let mut toc = None; for operation in &operations { toc = toc_provider.check_strict_mode(...).await?... } ... let mut results = Vec::with_capacity(operations.len()); ... for operation in operations { let current_update_result = match operation { UpdateOperation::Upsert(operation) => { do_upsert_points(...).await? ... } UpdateOperation::Delete(operation) => { do_delete_points(...).await? } ... } }' — accepted batches are applied strictly sequentially in the given order and one UpdateResult is collected per operation.
source_grounding.call_chain_traced: POST /collections/{name}/points/batch (actix route, update_api.rs:327) -> Json<UpdateOperations> whole-request untagged-enum deserialization (any non-matching op key, including the DOC-worded 'delete_points', rejects the ENTIRE request atomically -> 400 before any state change) -> update_batch handler -> do_batch_update_points (update.rs:752): strict-mode precheck of ALL operations first, then sequential for-loop application, one Vec<UpdateResult> entry per operation
source_grounding.note: validation_present: the source validates the entire operations array at deserialization — an unknown op key rejects the whole request with nothing applied (the observed 400 + GET 502 404). The claim's supposed 'half-apply' exists neither in source nor in behavior. The assertion's sequential-order and per-op-result clauses are implemented (sequential for-loop, per-op UpdateResult) and behaviorally confirmed by P1/P2. No explicit by-design marker is needed: the cited assertion is satisfied, not violated.
